title: Five Recurring Errors
subtitle: This is · a million · no repeated subject · What if I…? · enroll in

1.2: Fill in the blank with is or are

2.1: Practice: Fill in each blank with a, or leave it blank if no article is needed

3.2: Rewrite each sentence without repeating the subject

4.1: Practice: Rewrite each sentence as a clear question, removing just

5.1: Practice: Fill in each blank with in or for

6.1: Mixed Practice: Choose the correct option

slides.title: 1. Singular subject: "this"
slides.question: How do I introduce one item?
slides.summary: Use is with the singular subject this, and a singular noun for one item. Don't repeat the subject with it. Her example: not "This, it's a Philips headphones" but "This is a Philips headphone."

expressions.meaning: one item: This is my passport.
don't add "it" after "this".
this is singular, so the verb is is.
for more than one item: These are my keys.

items.question: Show a colleague your new laptop.
items.explain: This + is + one item. No "it" after "this".

items.question: Present a document in a meeting.
Point to two or more items.
items.explain: More than one item → these are + plural noun.

slides.title: 2. Articles: "a million dollars"
slides.question: What do I say before million?
slides.summary: Use a before million when you talk about an amount of money. Her example: not "If I won million dollars" but "If I won a million dollars, I would travel."

expressions.meaning: one million: always with "a" (or "one").
the same pattern: a hundred people, a thousand reais.
million starts with a consonant sound, so "a".
no "s" on million after a number.

items.question: What would you do with a million dollars?
items.explain: a million dollars. Second conditional: If I had…, I would…

items.question: Talk about a big amount at work.
Use the same pattern with hundred.
items.explain: a hundred, a thousand, a million: all with "a".

slides.title: 3. Don't repeat the subject
slides.question: How do I describe someone without repeating the subject?
slides.summary: When a noun is the subject, don't repeat it with a pronoun before the verb. Use the noun followed by the correct form of be. Her example: not "My wife, she's angry" but "My wife is angry."

expressions.meaning: My wife is angry. My manager is busy.
Our neighbors are friendly.
Portuguese allows this; English doesn't.
say: The students are…

items.question: Describe your manager.
items.explain: The noun is the subject: no "he" after it.

items.question: Describe a supplier.
items.explain: Noun + is. No "it" or "they" in between.

slides.title: 4. "What if I try…?" (no just)
slides.question: How do I make a suggestion with what if?
slides.summary: In her example, just is unnecessary. Start the question with What if I…, use the normal word order and finish with a question mark. Her example: not "What if just I try one more time here." but "What if I try one more time here?"

expressions.meaning: a suggestion: What if we call the office?
just in that position sounds wrong; drop it.
What if I try again? — start and end correctly.

items.question: Suggest calling the supplier.
items.explain: What if + I + verb. No "just". End with ?

items.question: Suggest trying again.
items.explain: Her structure: What if I try…?

slides.title: 5. Prepositions: "enroll in"
slides.question: How do I say I joined a course?
slides.summary: Use enroll in when you mean to join a course or program. Her example: not "I enrolled for a new MBA in AI" but "I enrolled in a new MBA in AI."

expressions.meaning: join it: I enrolled in an MBA.
use in for courses and programs.
American spelling: enroll, enrolled, enrolling.

items.question: Talk about a course you joined.
Give a deadline.
blocks: until the end of the month.

slides.title: Mixed practice and writing
slides.question: Can I use all five correctly together?
slides.summary: This part mixes the five points: This is + singular, a million dollars, a noun subject without a repeated pronoun, What if I try…? and enroll in. Then you write your own short paragraph using all of them.

expressions.meaning: one item, no "it".
always with "a".
no repeated pronoun.
no "just", end with ?
for courses and programs.

items.question: Show the course you want.
items.explain: This is + singular, and enroll in at the end.

items.question: Dream a little.
items.explain: a million dollars; noun subject (my family) + would.

items.question: Make a suggestion about studying.
items.explain: What if I + verb…? + enroll in.

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph about a goal, course, or opportunity you would pursue.
checklist: A sentence beginning with This is…
A sentence with a million dollars
A sentence with a noun subject and is, without repeating the subject with a pronoun
A question beginning with What if I try…?
A sentence using … (the file ends here — probably enroll in)
writing.model: This is my plan for next year. I want to enroll in an MBA program with a focus on supply chain. My manager is very supportive, and the company may pay part of the cost. Of course, if I had a million dollars, I would study abroad for a year! What if I try to get a scholarship first?
